The actions described in the paragraph present significant legal compliance issues, primarily concerning labor law violations.

First, the statement that employees were "already working the maximum hours permitted by local labor laws" and that the store extended hours without increasing pay suggests a direct violation of wage and hour regulations. In most jurisdictions, labor laws mandate overtime pay (typically 1.5 times the regular rate) for hours worked beyond a standard 40-hour workweek or daily limits. By extending hours without increasing pay, the employer is likely failing to compensate employees for overtime, which is illegal.

Second, the claim that this was a "one-time exception" does not exempt the employer from legal obligations. Labor laws generally apply regardless of the frequency or duration of the violation. Forcing employees to work beyond their legal maximums without proper compensation or, in some cases, without their consent (depending on specific local statutes regarding mandatory overtime), constitutes a breach of statutory duties.

Therefore, the described actions are non-compliant with standard legal standards regarding fair labor practices, specifically concerning overtime pay and maximum working hours.
